committed_fixes.cumulative_power: Accumulate in float64 on CPU and supported Torch devices, retaining public output dtype. Torch thresholds use float64 to match NumPy integer-arange promotion; MPS retains float32.
committed_fixes.native_cpu_chisq: Use existing point_chisq_code double real specialization with float64 shifts and accumulation. Compensate shortened pi using shifts times numpy.pi / 3.141592653. Final subtraction is double, with original public precision and correlation storage retained. No C/Cython/kernel edits.
committed_fixes.strain_and_measured_psd: For float32 CPU and Torch CPU/CUDA strain, promote each StrainSegments forward FFT and cast to original complex dtype. Promote measured-PSD strain before Welch, interpolation and inverse-spectrum truncation, restoring requested/default public precision. MPS behavior unchanged.

captured_bin_swap.interpretation: At this one trigger, changing bin edges with the input arrays fixed changes chi-squared by about 7.53; changing input arrays with the edges fixed changes it by about 0.0016. Bin selection accounts for the dominant captured discrepancy. The CPU float32 cumulative sum reproduces its recorded edges and underestimates its float64 cumulative total by 0.5241%; this is evidence of reference error, not a reason to relax parity budgets.
captured_bin_swap.scope: Causal diagnostic on one captured trigger; no qualification tolerances changed.

cuda_prefix_repeatability.float64_route_semantics: torch.cumsum(power, dtype=torch.float64).to(torch.float32); thresholds and search use float32.
cuda_prefix_repeatability.interpretation: The fixed float32 power vector produced three bin-edge vectors in 100 CUDA float32 scans. Float64 accumulation followed by float32 casting produced one edge vector in 100 scans. Its penultimate edge 362778 differs from the fully float64 CPU reference edge 362772, so repeatability alone does not establish numerical accuracy or a completed fix.
cuda_prefix_repeatability.scope: Repeatability diagnostic only; same fixed CUDA float32 power vector in both routes.

identical_input_chisq.interpretation: For these inputs, native float32 accumulation/phase evaluation is inaccurate against direct complex128. Float64 arithmetic with the original pi constant still leaves measurable error; the full-precision-pi variant agrees to about 1.2e-9, and Torch CPU with identical inputs agrees to about 1.8e-6. This does not certify all Torch campaign outputs.
identical_input_chisq.scope: One template, four captured CPU segments, eight trigger samples; fixed captured correlation, normalization, indices and CPU bin edges. Native variants were compiled locally and do not reproduce Linux float32 results bitwise.

initial_corrected_cli_comparison.interpretation: At segment length 512, all 475 trigger identities match for both backends and SNR/phase/normalization pass. Torch CPU passes every metric. CUDA still has 302 chi-squared violations, maximum absolute error 0.7212486267089844. This remains a blocker; no corrected full-CLI parity pass or performance result is claimed.

interpretation_limits: One captured trigger demonstrates the dominant bin effect; public float32 rounding and discrete frequency-cell placement remain.
The 100-repeat double-accumulation control retained float32 thresholds. Stable output is not proof of exact agreement with the wholly float64 reference.
Locally compiled native float32 does not reproduce Linux bitwise; controlled precision/pi comparisons isolate phase error without proving bitwise portability.
SNR/PSD v2 covers one template and segment, only two unclustered samples above 5.5, and direct float64 normalization. That point is not the campaign worst SNR/phase failure.
The old CPU reference changes. These controls establish mechanisms, not accuracy for every full-bank trigger.
